{"ranking":[],"explanation":"No candidate edit addresses the core defect. The trace shows cycle 5: tkeep=1, tlast=1, tready=1, tvalid=1, rst=0. Original RTL at line 84 enters the tlast branch, sets frame_len_valid_next=1, frame_next=0, then at line 95 (KEEP_ENABLE=1) runs the bit-count loop. The loop condition `monitor_axis_tkeep == ({KEEP_WIDTH{1'b1}}) >> (KEEP_WIDTH-i)` with KEEP_WIDTH=8 evaluates true for i=0 (0x00==0x00) and i=1 (0x01==0x01), so bit_cnt=1, frame_len_next becomes 1. Expected frame_len is 1 and matches.

The mismatch says actual frame_len=3, meaning bit_cnt=3 was added. That requires the loop to match at i=3, i.e. mask 0x07, but tkeep=0x01. Therefore the defect is the mask expression `({KEEP_WIDTH{1'b1}}) >> (KEEP_WIDTH-i)` which produces right-justified masks 0x00,0x01,0x03,0x07… The contract says “Supported TKEEP values are contiguous low-order ones (2^k-1, including zero)” i.e. exactly those masks, but the loop assigns bit_cnt = i, so for mask 0x01 (k=1) it yields i=1 → correct; for mask 0x03 (k=2) it yields i=2 → correct. The problem is the loop also matches i=0 for all-zero tkeep, which adds 0. That is harmless.

Why actual=3? Only if the loop ran three times or bit_cnt accumulated across cycles. The original combinational block re-initializes bit_cnt=0 each evaluation, so no accumulation. The only way to get +3 in one cycle is if the loop condition matched i=3. With tkeep=0x01 that cannot happen.

Since every candidate only adds extra boolean guards to existing conditions (lines 81,84,88,95,98) and none rewrites the mask formula or the loop index-to-count mapping, none can change bit_cnt from 1 to 3. The failure is in the arithmetic encoding of the mask-to-count conversion, which no offered patch touches. Therefore no candidate from the supplied list can fix the observed mismatch."}
